clue.text: Diet of family in South American city

definitions.note: used as a modifier, as in a diet or low-fat drink

indicators.note: the family word is placed in the middle of the city letters, cut open after the S

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for South
NY, New York, is the great American city
kin are one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: A family's eating regime in some South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' looks like a noun but works as an adjective: a skinny latte is the low-fat, diet version.
explanation.definitionFit: On café menus, skinny describes the reduced-fat or low-calorie version of a drink, the slimming option.

clue.text: Fold to add shape

parts.note: a fold is a pen or enclosure for sheep
to tag on is to add something at the end

explanation.surface: Origami instructions: fold the paper to add a shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fold' is not a verb here but a sheep enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-sided polygon is a geometric figure, hence a shape.

clue.text: Outcry as Oxford player crows

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsperson who has represented Oxford (or Cambridge) University
a group of crows is called a murder

explanation.surface: An Oxford sportsman crowing over victory causes protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crows' looks like a verb (boasts) but is the birds: the collective noun for crows is a murder.
explanation.definitionFit: To scream this phrase is to make a loud, furious protest, so it means an uproar or outcry.

clue.text: Strangle fish with bad cut

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

indicators.note: cut means the word for bad loses its last letter

parts.note: bad food is rotten

explanation.surface: A grisly instruction: throttle a fish with a poor cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims ROTTEN to ROTTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrotte is a wire or cord used for throttling, and as a verb it means to kill by choking.

clue.text: Helping model to get work

parts.note: a doll is a model of a person
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Giving a model some help to find a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a large spoonful of food, a serving or portion.

clue.text: Delivery that must be repeated with fish

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's delivery that has to be sent again, with fish.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a ball bowled out of the batter's reach is called a wide; it adds a run and must be bowled again.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bowled ball beyond the batter's reach does not count and has to be re-bowled.

clue.text: Limb inserted into upset male animal

indicators.note: the limb word is put inside the other piece
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: An arm pushed into an angry male creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' in a down clue means flipped upside down, so the male cat is read backwards before the limb is put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmot is a burrowing rodent of the squirrel family, a mountain-dwelling mammal.

clue.text: Lay odds of trek maps being seen before test

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece comes before, above, the exam
the odd-numbered letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: Betting odds on hiking maps before an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds of' takes letters 1, 3, 5, 7 of TREK MAPS: TEMP. 'Lay' looks like a betting verb, beside 'odds', but it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporal can mean secular, relating to worldly rather than church affairs, as lay people are not clergy.

clue.text: Barge over knight, and prepare to be knighted?

indicators.note: the barge word goes over, covering, the knight letter

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed barge, as used on the Tyne
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A barge sails over a knight, who then readies for an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barge' looks like a verb (push rudely) but is a boat, the keel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone being dubbed goes down on one knee before the monarch, which is the posture asked for.

clue.text: Desperate to be a man, I feel hatred

indicators.note: something desperate is in a frantic, disordered state, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone longing to be a man feels a burning hatred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperate' rearranges TOBEAMANI.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe or detest, so the verb means feeling hatred towards something.

clue.text: Idiot about to make ingredient of rocket fuel

parts.note: a nit is a fool, a nitwit
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A fool is about to brew some rocket fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'going to'; 'about' is RE and 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre (potassium nitrate) is an oxidiser in gunpowder and early rocket propellants.

clue.text: 3D representation of female with half-ripped pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or bad, so the letters are in a bad, jumbled order
half means the first three of the six letters are taken

explanation.surface: A three-dimensional image of a woman whose underwear is half torn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear but is the slang adjective for rubbish, signalling FEMALE plus RIP rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief map shows hills and valleys in raised form, a three-dimensional model of terrain.

clue.text: Heading west, Spanish artist almost damaged culture

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west means read right to left
almost means the painter's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Goya was a Spanish painter
hurt means damaged or harmed

explanation.surface: A Spanish painter going west nearly ruined civilisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims GOYA to GOY and 'Heading west' turns it to YOG. 'culture' is not civilisation but a bacterial culture.
explanation.definitionFit: This fermented milk product is made with a live bacterial culture, so it is itself called a culture.

clue.text: Continue to block a medical treatment

indicators.note: the word for continue sits inside, blocking the other piece

parts.note: per can mean a, as in five pounds a day
to last is to continue or endure

explanation.surface: Carry on obstructing a course of treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' stands for PER (as in 'so much per day'); LAST goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticking dressing or a cast for a broken limb is applied as a medical remedy.

clue.text: Blair dared to transform aid to keep seafarer afloat

indicators.note: to transform letters is to change them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Tony Blair boldly overhauled aid for sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transform' rearranges BLAIRDARED. The seafarer is a fish, whose gas-filled sac keeps it buoyant.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish have a gas-filled sac (swim bladder) that controls buoyancy, so it keeps a sea creature afloat.

clue.text: German article on, say, lust and introduction to eroticism is indefinitely postponed

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after

parts.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins, an example of a sin

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter

parts.note: die is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A German writes about lust and the beginnings of eroticism, then postpones it forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks lust as one example of a sin; 'on' in an across clue puts the German article last.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin legal phrase means without a day fixed, so adjourned with no date for resuming.

clue.text: Representative limbos extremely carefully at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are mixed up
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Careful limbo dancers performing on a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives CY from 'carefully'; with LIMBOS, 'at sea' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something symbolic stands for or represents something else, as an emblem does.

clue.text: Dalibor's talent stopped by prison

indicators.note: the answer is held, stopped up, by the clue's words around it

explanation.surface: Dalibor's talent is halted by a jail sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies inside 'DaliBOR'S TALent'.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a British institution for young offenders, a youth jail.

clue.text: Squint, as overbearing editor receives tip from Eccles

definitions.note: used as an adjective, describing eyes that look in different directions

indicators.note: the letter is received into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: bossy means overbearing or domineering

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A domineering editor squints at a note from Eccles, the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives' puts E inside BOSSYED, after BOSS. Eccles is the setter of this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Boss-eyed is British informal for cross-eyed or having a cast in one eye, a strabismus.

clue.text: Hearing range in rehearsal

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
a run is a range or series, as in a run of numbers or an animal's run

explanation.surface: Checking the range of one's hearing during practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice attempt before the real thing is a test run, a dress rehearsal.

clue.text: Rodent smell surrounds retrograde animal sanctuary

indicators.note: the smell word goes all round the other piece

parts.note: must is a musty, mouldy smell

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so read in reverse

parts.note: Noah's ark was a refuge for the animals

explanation.surface: A stink surrounds a run-down animal refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrograde' reverses Noah's ark. 'smell' tempts as musk, but the wordplay needs must, a musty odour.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large North American water rodent, prized for its fur.

clue.text: Increase in temperature in inadequate rough hut

indicators.note: temperature going up means cold, C, becomes hot, H, inside the word

parts.note: scanty means insufficient or inadequate

explanation.surface: A heatwave in a shabby little cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: C (cold) and H (hot) are the tap labels; raising the temperature swaps C for H.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a crude, ramshackle dwelling, as in a shanty town.

clue.text: Sad tidings to start with: Corona, possibly, has returned

indicators.note: to start with means the first letter of the word
in a down clue returned means read backwards

parts.note: a corona is a type of long cigar, so this is one example

explanation.surface: Sad news at first: the coronavirus has come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corona' suggests the virus but is the cigar; 'has returned' turns it to RAGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic means deeply distressing, causing great sorrow, hence sad.

clue.text: Lane close to Kent bores drunk musician

indicators.note: the character's name bores into the drunkard word, sitting within it

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
Lois Lane is the reporter close to Clark Kent in the Superman stories

explanation.surface: A lane near the end of Kent, where a drunken performer drones on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to Kent' looks like the last letter of Kent, but Lane close to Kent is Lois Lane, Superman's colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A soloist is a performer who plays or sings alone, a kind of musician.

clue.text: Felt tattooist up to check rumours

definitions.note: plural here, while the answer is a mass noun for gossip

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, backwards
the clue's words check, hold back, the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A tattooist felt obliged to check gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to check' finds ELTTAT inside 'fELT TATtooist'; 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattle is idle talk or gossip about other people's affairs, the stuff rumours are made of.

clue.text: Agreed on a fresh drink

indicators.note: fresh means new, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Settling on a new beverage by agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges AGREEDONA; it looks like it describes the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fruit-flavoured soft drink, a citrus beverage.

clue.text: He perhaps gets heroin cut

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium, an example of a gas
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A man getting hold of heroin that has been adulterated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a man but is helium. 'cut', next to heroin, suggests diluted drugs, but means a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash is a long, deep wound or slash, so a cut.

clue.text: Expert tours large Dutch city

indicators.note: the expert word goes round the large letter

parts.note: deft means skilful, expert
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A specialist guide takes groups round a big Dutch city.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is a town in South Holland famous for blue-and-white pottery.

clue.text: Queen barred from engaging, mostly, with bit of effervescence in bowel

indicators.note: the queen letters are barred, kept out, of the word
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: engaging means interesting or absorbing
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

indicators.note: a bit of the word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: The Queen banned from an engagement, with fizz in her digestive system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims INTERESTING to INTERESTIN; 'barred from' removes ER to leave INTESTIN; 'bit of' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: The bowel is the gut, the long tube of the lower digestive tract.

clue.text: Even English game bird passes over India

indicators.note: passes over means skips or leaves out the India letter

parts.note: the quail is a small game bird
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An English game bird flies over India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passes over' looks like flight but means skipping: QUAIL loses I.
explanation.definitionFit: Equal and even both mean level, balanced, with neither side ahead.
